'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Gaza war]]
**The [[Israel]]i [[Security Cabinet of Israel|Security Cabinet]] approves [[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]]'s plan to capture [[Gaza City]] with the stated objective of defeating [[Hamas]], while supposedly ensuring the provision of [[humanitarian aid]] to civilians outside the areas of combat. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-08-08/israel-security-cabinet-approves-pm-s-plan-to-seize-gaza-city-me26un7f (Bloomberg)]
**[[Germany]] announces it will halt weapon shipments to Israel that could be used in Gaza "until further notice" in light of Israel's plan to fully [[Military occupation|militarily occupy]] [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]. [https://apnews.com/article/germany-mideast-weapons-b957e28b73ee94ed33fbd2d4e4d36246 (AP)]
**The [[Israel Defense Forces]] begins massing [[Israeli Ground Forces|troops]] and [[Armored Corps (Israel)|tanks]] on the [[Gaza–Israel barrier|border with Gaza]] ahead of an expected major ground offensive. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/middle-east/ground-invasion-in-gaza-israel-military-building-up-troops-equipment-near-border-report/articleshow/123183462.cms (''The Times of India'')]
*[[Kivu conflict]]
**[[M23 campaign (2022–present)|M23 campaign]]
***[[Volker Türk]], the [[Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights|UN high commissioner for human rights]], reports that [[M23 rebels]] have killed over 319 civilians in July. M23 president [[Bertrand Bisimwa]] said the group would investigate the claim. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/8/6/m23-rebels-killed-319-civilians-in-east-dr-congo-in-july-un-says (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/m23-rebels-killed-319-civilians-east-congo-july-un-rights-chief-says-2025-08-06/ (Reuters)]
*[[Insurgency in Balochistan]]
**At least 33 [[Pakistani Taliban]] [[militant]]s are killed in an overnight operation near the [[Afghanistan]] border in [[Zhob]], [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/world/article/pakistani-forces-kill-33-militants-in-overnight-operation-near-afghan-border/ (CTV News)]
*[[War on drugs]]
**[[U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]] signs an [[executive order]] commanding the [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. military]] and other sectors of the [[Federal government of the United States|federal government]] to take action against [[Latin America]]n [[drug cartels]] [[United States Department of State list of Foreign Terrorist Organizations|designated as terrorist organisations]], such as [[Tren de Aragua]] and [[MS-13]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/8/8/trump-signs-order-authorising-military-action-against-cartels-reports (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2025/08/08/us/trump-military-drug-cartels.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*A bus carrying mourners back home from a funeral in [[Kisumu]], [[Kenya]], overturns and plunges into a ditch, killing at least 21 people. [https://www.msn.com/en-gb/news/world/a-bus-carrying-mourners-from-a-funeral-overturns-in-kenya-killing-21-people/ar-AA1KaN3Y?ocid=msedgdhp&pc=U531&cvid=46626e408c0048a591c5168ba0abbf06&ei=24 (MSN)]
*A bus and a truck collide head-on near [[Lucas do Rio Verde]], [[Mato Grosso]], [[Brazil]], killing 11 people and injuring 45 others. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/bus-collision-with-truck-kills-11-injures-45-brazil-2025-08-09/ (Reuters)]
*At least 15 people are killed and 33 others are missing following a flash flood in [[Yuzhong County]], [[Gansu]], [[China]]. [https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202508/09/WS689738e5a310724b60020cb1.html (''China Daily'')]
*At least 30 people are injured when a passenger train derails on the Kerman–Zarand railway path near [[Siriz]], [[Kerman province]], [[Iran]]. [https://tribune.com.pk/story/2560356/at-least-30-injured-after-train-derails-in-southern-iran (''The Express Tribune'')] [https://caliber.az/en/post/iran-passenger-train-derails-in-kerman-all-safe (Caliber)]
*A fire breaks out at the [[Mosque–Cathedral of Córdoba]] in [[Andalusia]], [[Spain]], due to a short circuit. The roof of a chapel collapses, but the fire is extinguished with no further damage. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/aug/08/fire-breaks-out-at-cordobas-ancient-mosque-turned-cathedral-la-mezquita (''The Guardian'')] [https://elpais.com/cultura/2025-08-09/colapsa-el-techo-de-la-capilla-donde-se-origino-el-incendio-de-la-mezquita.html (''El País'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Armenia–Azerbaijan relations]]
**[[Armenia–Azerbaijan peace agreement]]
***The leaders of [[Armenia]] and [[Azerbaijan]] plan to sign a joint declaration at the [[White House]] in [[Washington, D.C.]], [[United States]], committing to a peace deal facilitated by the [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] that would end nearly four decades of conflict between the two countries. [https://www.cnn.com/2025/08/08/politics/strategic-armenia-azerbaijan-corridor-named-after-trump (CNN)]
***Armenia agrees to grant the U.S. exclusive development rights in the [[Zangezur corridor]] for 99 years. The U.S. would sublease to a consortium to develop rail, oil, gas, and fiber optic lines along the 27-mile (43km) corridor. [https://www.politico.com/news/2025/08/07/us-deal-armenia-azerbaijan-00499285 (Politico)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2025 Indian electoral controversy]]
**[[Rahul Gandhi]], the [[Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha]] alleges an electoral fraud(vote chori) done by the [[Election Commission of India]] in connection with the [[Bharatiya Janata Party|BJP]] in multiple elections across [[India]].
[https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/rahul-gandhi-alleges-massive-voter-fraud-2024-lok-sabha-elections-bjp-election-commission-of-india/article69904858.ece (The Hindu)]
*[[2025 Anaconda shooting]]
**The suspected perpetrator of the bar shooting that killed four people last week in [[Anaconda, Montana|Anaconda]], [[Montana]], United States, is arrested. [https://www.krtv.com/news/crime-and-courts/anaconda-shootings-suspect-arrested (KRTV-TV)] 
*[[2024 South Korean martial law crisis]]
**The [[Judiciary of South Korea|Seoul Central District Court]] rejects a petition brought by former [[Ministry of the Interior and Safety|interior minister]] [[Lee Sang-min (lawyer)|Lee Sang-min]] regarding the arrest warrant against him over his alleged involvement in former [[President of South Korea|president]] [[Yoon Suk Yeol]]'s martial law attempt on December 3, 2024. [https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/southkorea/law-crime/20250808/court-dismisses-ex-interior-ministers-petition-against-arrest (''The Korea Times'')]
*A police officer and the perpetrator are killed, and another officer suffers non-life-threatening injuries, in a shooting at the [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention|CDC]] building near [[Emory University]] in [[Atlanta]], [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], United States. [https://www.cnn.com/us/live-news/active-shooter-emory-university?t=1754695635612 (CNN)] [https://www.fox5atlanta.com/news/centers-disease-control-active-shooter-emory-university (WAGA-TV)]
*The [[Uganda High Court]] denies bail to opposition figure [[Kizza Besigye]], who faces treason charges, ruling that the 180-day period for mandatory release began when his case was transferred to a civilian court in February, leaving him 12 days short of eligibility. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/ugandan-court-denies-bail-veteran-opposition-leader-treason-case-2025-08-08/ (Reuters)]
*[[Portugal]]'s [[Constitutional Court (Portugal)|Constitutional Court]] blocks a [[Assembly of the Republic (Portugal)|parliamentary]] bill that would require most legally resident [[Immigration to Portugal|immigrants]] to wait two years before applying for [[family reunification]], ruling that it violates [[Constitution of Portugal|constitutional]] protections for family unity. [https://www.reuters.com/world/portugals-top-court-blocks-bill-restricting-immigration-2025-08-09/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Belarus|Belarusian]] [[President of Belarus|president]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] says that his 7th term will be his last, and hints that he will not run in the upcoming 2030 presidential election. [https://www.trtworld.com/article/cfa4ce779592 (TRT World)]
*[[Brazil]]ian [[President of Brazil|president]] [[Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva]] vetoes 63 provisions of a [[Brazilian National Congress|congressional]] bill revising [[Environmental governance in Brazil|environmental licensing rules]], removing measures that would have expanded fast-tracking of projects in sensitive areas such as the [[Amazon rainforest]]. [https://apnews.com/article/brazil-lula-veto-environment-licensing-bill-ecfc20b67ce7b4fbaeb2f14ba9f787ee (AP)]
